_meta.description: Official registries where lost and abandoned retirement accounts are reported. The 'excludes' and 'requires' fields are what make this more useful than the government's own pages.
_meta.verifyNote: All URLs are link-checked by build/qa.js.

registries.name: DOL Retirement Savings Lost & Found
registries.covers: Private-sector employer and union retirement plans, built from information plans report to the IRS.
registries.excludes: Church plans and government plans. Coverage is not comprehensive — a 'nothing found' result does not mean you have no lost accounts.
registries.requires: Identity verification through Login.gov: your legal name, date of birth, Social Security number, a mobile device, and photos of the front and back of a valid driver's license or state ID.
registries.notes: Created by the SECURE 2.0 Act. This is the newest and most authoritative federal starting point, but the identity-verification step stops many people — expect it before you begin.

registries.name: National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits
registries.covers: Retirement plan benefits that participating employers have voluntarily reported as unclaimed.
registries.excludes: Any plan whose employer did not choose to register with the service. This is voluntary, so coverage is partial.
registries.requires: Your Social Security number to run a search.
registries.notes: Private and voluntary, not a government database. Quick to check and worth doing, but never treat an empty result as conclusive.

registries.name: PBGC Unclaimed Pensions
registries.covers: Unclaimed benefits from traditional defined benefit pension plans that PBGC has taken over, typically after the sponsoring company failed.
registries.excludes: 401(k) and other defined contribution accounts. This is pensions only.
registries.requires: Name and, helpfully, the former employer's name. No SSN needed for the initial search.
registries.notes: Search this if you or a relative had a traditional pension, especially from a company that went bankrupt.

registries.name: State Unclaimed Property (MissingMoney)
registries.covers: Cash and securities turned over to states when accounts go dormant, including cashed-out retirement balances.
registries.excludes: Not every state participates in MissingMoney, and some states' data lags. Always also check each state's own site directly.
registries.requires: Just your name. This is public record — no SSN required to search.
registries.notes: The easiest place to start because it needs no identity verification. Search every state you have ever lived or worked in, and check maiden and former names.

registries.name: DOL Form 5500 / EFAST Filing Search
registries.covers: Annual reports filed by employer retirement plans, which name the plan administrator and plan sponsor contacts.
registries.excludes: Very small plans may have limited filing requirements, and filings can lag by a year or more.
registries.requires: The former employer's name. No personal information needed.
registries.notes: This is the professional's tool. When a company merged, was acquired, or closed, the Form 5500 tells you who is legally responsible for the plan today — which is who you actually need to call.

registries.name: DOL Benefits Advisors (EBSA)
registries.operator: Employee Benefits Security Administration, U.S. Department of Labor
registries.covers: Free one-on-one help from federal benefits advisors when a plan will not respond or you cannot identify an administrator.
registries.excludes: They assist and investigate; they do not maintain a searchable balance database.
registries.notes: Genuinely free federal help that almost nobody uses. If a plan is stonewalling you, this is the escalation path.
